name: Erodium

project_scope.selection_mode: two approved Master Plant Pool species; genus framework only
project_scope.species_installation: Approved Taxa Installer only; neither species appears in latest manifest
project_scope.range_note: Preserve separate existing native-range states; no new county PASS or native metric inferred.

look_here_first: Start with a full mature leaf: is it pinnately compound with many deeply cut leaflets, or a single rounded/ovate blade with 3–5 lobes? Confirm Erodium from a flower with five fertile stamens and five sterile staminodes, then from the long-beaked five-part fruit.
shared_genus_traits: Herbaceous annuals or short-lived herbs with stipulate leaves, often in a basal rosette.
Flowers usually have five free sepals and five free petals; five fertile stamens plus five staminodes are characteristic.
Fruits are elongated beaked schizocarps separating into five one-seeded mericarps, each with a hygroscopically coiling awn.

species_comparison_matrix.Erodium cicutarium: Pinnately compound leaf with numerous leaflets; leaflets deeply pinnately lobed or cut, fernlike in outline.
species_comparison_matrix.Erodium texanum: Simple blade, ovate to rounded, usually 3–5 broad lobes with toothed margins; not a series of separate leaflets.
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_see: Lay entire leaf flat; label rachis, individual leaflets, and lobes. Compare basal mature leaves, not cotyledons.
Photograph intact peduncle and all pedicels; overlap at 2–3 flowers means not decisive.

species_comparison_matrix.Erodium cicutarium: Five fertile stamens, five staminodes; elongated beak and five mericarps.
species_comparison_matrix.Erodium texanum: Same genus architecture; do not use a long beak by itself to split species.
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_see: Flower-center macro with anthers counted; ripe fruit macro showing beak, mericarps, and spiral awn.

species_comparison_matrix.Erodium cicutarium: Pink-purple petals and reddish hairy stems possible.
species_comparison_matrix.Erodium texanum: Pink-purple petals and reddish hairy stems possible.
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_see: Treat color and stem tint as context only.

decision_sequence: Find a complete mature leaf, including its attachment: many discrete leaflets on a rachis → E. cicutarium; one broadly lobed blade → E. texanum.
Check multiple leaves on the same individual and photograph an intact flowering cluster; 2–3 flowers overlaps both.
Verify five fertile stamens plus five staminodes and a five-mericarpped beaked fruit when available; these confirm Erodium rather than either species.
If only flowers or a detached fruit are available, retain Erodium sp. rather than forcing a species.
overlap_cautions: Both species may have pink-purple flowers, reddish stems, a low spreading habit, and long beaked fruits.
Flower-cluster counts overlap; no single flower color or beak-length observation should determine the species.

The existing Joey video reference labeled E. texanum mentions 'dissected leaves'. Verify the exact photographed plant and whether the foliage is actually a simple lobed blade before treating that frame as diagnostic evidence.
Learner admission from the approved source pool is not a native-range certification; neither taxon is installed canonically.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.separate: Geranium typically has ten fertile stamens; Erodium has five fertile stamens plus five staminodes. Check flower center and fruit; both can have lobed leaves.
Use mature beaked schizocarp and stamen arrangement rather than flower color alone.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Matched mature basal leaves with a scale; annotate pinnate rachis/leaflets vs single 3–5-lobed blade
Matched flower-center macros marking five anther-bearing stamens and five staminodes
Long-beaked immature and mature fruits, five mericarps and coiled awns with scale
Intact flowering clusters showing all pedicels and count
